title: Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES)
summary: 16-bit home video game console famous for Mode 7 pseudo-3D scaling, SPC700 audio chip, and legendary 2D sprite graphics masterpieces.
facts: Released in Japan as Super Famicom in November 1990 and North America in August 1991.
Mode 7 graphics hardware mode enabled rotation and scaling of background layers.
Included games enhanced with coprocessor expansion chips like the Super FX chip in Star Fox.

title: Sony PlayStation (PS1)
summary: 32-bit CD-ROM home console designed by Ken Kutaragi that popularized 3D gaming, optical disc media, and memory cards for saving progress.
facts: Originally conceived as a CD-ROM add-on for the Super Nintendo before Sony developed it independently.
Became the first home console to ship over 100 million units worldwide.
Introduced DualAnalog and DualShock controller with twin analog thumbsticks and haptic vibration.

title: Nintendo 64 (N64)
summary: 64-bit home video game console powered by NEC VR4300 CPU and Silicon Graphics (SGI) RCP graphics chip, featuring four controller ports and analog stick.
facts: Launched alongside Super Mario 64, establishing standard 3D platforming controls.
Used ROM cartridge format providing fast loading times despite higher media manufacturing costs.
Standardized 4-player split-screen local multiplayer couch gaming.

title: Sega Saturn
summary: 32-bit dual-CPU CD-ROM home video game console renowned for superb 2D arcade ports and quad-based 3D graphics architecture.
facts: Surprise early North American launch at E3 1995 for $399.
Featured dual Hitachi SH-2 32-bit RISC processors.
Acclaimed in Japan for 2D arcade games and fighting game ports with RAM expansion cartridges.

title: Sega Dreamcast
summary: 128-bit sixth-generation console featuring PowerVR2 graphics, GD-ROM optical discs, and built-in 56k dial-up modem for online gaming.
facts: Launched in Japan in Nov 1998 and US on the famous 9/9/99 date for $199.
Introduced the VMU (Visual Memory Unit) memory card with built-in LCD screen.
First console to offer built-in internet modem and web browser out of the box.
